purpose: Test whether the connection cost axis gives the optimiser something to trade. v2.38.0 added cited latency and energy per connection type; an axis nobody optimises over is decoration. Two runs, same space, same budget, same evaluation seed, one objective changed.

method.objective_a: wire cost + capability coverage (the Phase 3 shape)
method.objective_b: objective A + latency penalty + energy penalty
method.search_space: unit names whose internal wiring names connection types

type_granularity.note: Unit granularity is where the library's own units live and it is NOT testable: only 14 of 115 units have every connection type on the latency axis. The type-level run is the one with authority, and the two are never pooled.

verdict: WEAK: the two objectives never picked the same organism, but neither is better on latency. The axis reshuffles the search without steering it, which is noise dressed as a result.

direction_check.note: The claim under test is 'the axis steers the optimiser'. A run where the latency penalty ends up with HIGHER latency has failed regardless of how many seeds picked a different topology.

caveat: This measures whether the OPTIMISER RESPONDS to the axis, not whether the outcome beats biology. Phase 3's negative computation result is untouched by this script and nothing here revises it.
Latency is summed from cited ranges, so every figure is a band. A topology containing an `unknown`-latency type has no latency figure and is reported as such, never assigned a default.

The two fitness values are NOT comparable across objectives: each is normalised inside its own objective, so `cost_aware` scores lower by construction (it carries two extra penalty terms). Only the topologies and the axis values are compared.
The search space is unit names, not connection types. A future version should let the GA pick connection types directly; this one can only trade at the granularity the unit library offers.
